Ask questions about a GitHub repo without cloning it

AUTHOR · XERJ documentation team · REVIEWED BY · XERJ engineering team · PUBLISHED · 2026-10-19 · UPDATED · 2026-10-20

TL;DR — To ask questions about a GitHub repo without cloning it, run xerj ask "your question". If the repo is in the Corpus Hub catalogue, xerj pulls a signed, pre-indexed pack and answers with file:line, the pinned commit and the licence. Measured 2026-10-19: first answer 2,356 ms including the download, later answers 30 to 40 ms.

PASTE THIS TO YOUR AI AGENT — IT DOES THE REST Read https://xerj.org/llms.txt. Install xerj, then answer my question about the library with xerj ask (add --corpus and --def for an exact symbol). Quote the corpus, the pinned commit, the file:line and the licence line it prints, and say so when it exits 1 with no match.
RUN THIS XERJ COMMAND curl -fsSL https://xerj.org/get | sh Install the release binary into ~/.local/bin.
RUN THIS XERJ COMMAND xerj ask "how does snappy decompress a literal" Route the question to a corpus, pull its signed pack once and answer with file:line.
RUN THIS XERJ COMMAND xerj ask --corpus zstd --def ZSTD_CLEVEL_DEFAULT --json Exact definition lookup in one corpus, as JSON with the pin, licence class and hits.
RUN THIS XERJ COMMAND xerj hub status List cached packs, the automatic node and the hosted setting.

Run it

This ran in a fresh HOME with v1.0.0-rc.97. No node was running. xerj ask started a node on port 9300, pulled the snappy pack and answered.

curl -fsSL https://xerj.org/get | sh
xerj ask "how does snappy decompress a literal"

xerj hub status shows what is cached and where the node runs:

hosted: auto
last sync: never

The exit code tells an agent the result. 0 is answered, 1 is no match and 2 is an unknown corpus. 3 is a failed pack check and 4 is more than one matching corpus.

The catalogue the client verified was signed with ed25519 and generated on 2026-10-18 with 14 corpora. Packs are downloaded from GitHub Releases of xerj-org/xerj, so the GitHub API is not involved.

When not to use xerj

  • The repo is not in the catalogue. Clone it and use xerj autoindex; zero-setup asking for any source is issue #1800.
  • You need today's code. Packs are pinned; these were 18 days old, and each answer prints the age.
  • The question must not leave the machine and you have not set --offline or --hosted off.
  • You want to copy code from an approach-only corpus into your project. The licence class says read, do not copy.

FAQ

How can I ask questions about a GitHub repo without cloning it?

If the repo is in the Corpus Hub catalogue, run xerj ask "your question". xerj downloads a signed pack that is already indexed, at a pinned commit, and answers with file:line. Nothing is cloned or indexed on your machine.

Which repos can I ask about?

The signed catalogue generated on 2026-10-18 lists 14 corpora, including lz4, snappy, zstd, aiohttp and astro. hub.xerj.org lists 513 live corpora in its registry, but only catalogue entries have packs xerj ask can pull.

Can I search a GitHub repo without cloning if it is not in the catalogue?

Not with xerj today. Clone it and run xerj autoindex. Pointing xerj ask at any repository is tracked as issue #1800, which is open.

Does my question leave my machine?

It can. --hosted auto is the default: off inside a git repository, on elsewhere. Pass --offline or --hosted off to answer only from cached packs. Our runs printed answered from: local pack.

Can Claude Code or Cursor use this over MCP?

Yes. xerj mcp serves xerj_hub_find, xerj_hub_def and xerj_hub_ask. They answer from packs already on the machine and never download one; they name the xerj hub pull line instead.

Can I copy the code it shows?

Check the licence line. Each answer prints the SPDX licence and a class. zstd and lz4 are approach-only, and the output says read, do not copy.
